capabilities.title: Choose between LoRA, QLoRA, and full fine-tuning
capabilities.summary: Pick the fine-tuning strategy from model size, GPU memory budget, and acceptable quality trade-off.

when: about to fine-tune a 7B-70B LLM
GPU memory is a limiting factor for training
deciding whether parameter-efficient fine-tuning is appropriate
avoid_when: training a small model (<1B parameters) — full fine-tuning is preferred
maximum quality is required and compute budget is available
significant domain shift requires updating all model weights

steps: Choose LoRA when fine-tuning 7B-70B models on consumer GPUs (RTX 4090, A100), when you need small swappable adapters (~6MB vs a 14-16GB full model), or when deploying multiple task-specific variants from one base model.
Choose QLoRA (LoRA + 4-bit quantization) when memory is the primary constraint — e.g. fitting a 70B model on a single 24GB GPU — and a ~5% quality trade-off vs full fine-tuning is acceptable.
Choose full fine-tuning when the model is small (<1B params), when maximum quality is required with compute to spare, or when a large domain shift requires updating all weights.
Memory reference (Llama 3.1 8B): full FT 60+ GB; LoRA r=16 ~18 GB; QLoRA r=16 ~6 GB; IA3 ~16 GB. Trainable params: LoRA/QLoRA ~0.1-1%, IA3 ~0.01%.
Quality reference (MMLU): LoRA and QLoRA stay within ~1-2 points of full FT (e.g. Llama 2-7B: full 45.3, LoRA 44.8, QLoRA 44.1).

expected_outcomes: LoRA/QLoRA train <1% of parameters (~0.17% for an 8B model) with minor accuracy loss
QLoRA lets a 70B model fit on a single 24GB GPU at a ~5% quality trade-off

capabilities.title: Select LoRA rank, alpha, and target modules
capabilities.summary: Choose r, lora_alpha, and target_modules from capacity guidance and the model's architecture.

when: configuring a LoraConfig for a training run
trading LoRA capacity against memory
adapting LoRA to a specific model architecture (Llama, GPT-2, Falcon, BLOOM, ...)
avoid_when: using a non-LoRA PEFT method (e.g. IA3, prefix tuning) whose config uses different fields

steps: Start with r=8-16; increase to r=32-64 for complex tasks, domain adaptation, or 70B models. Rank guide: r=8 (~7M params, good, recommended start), r=16 (~14M, better, general fine-tuning), r=32/64 (higher capacity, more memory).
Set lora_alpha = 2 * r as the default (e.g. r=16 -> alpha=32). Use alpha=r for a conservative (lower effective LR) effect, or a larger alpha for a more aggressive effect.

Target attention + MLP layers for best quality/efficiency. Llama/Mistral/Qwen: q_proj, v_proj, k_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj. GPT-2/GPT-Neo: c_attn, c_proj, c_fc. Falcon/BLOOM: query_key_value, dense, dense_h_to_4h, dense_4h_to_h.
Use target_modules="all-linear" (PEFT 0.6.0+) to auto-detect and target all linear layers.
Set lora_dropout ~0.05 and bias="none" as defaults.

expected_outcomes: Higher rank yields more capacity/quality at higher memory cost
Targeting attention + MLP layers gives the best quality/efficiency balance

capabilities.title: Fine-tune an LLM with standard LoRA
capabilities.summary: Attach a LoRA adapter to a base causal LM and train it with the HuggingFace Trainer, saving the adapter only.

when: fine-tuning a 7B-70B model that fits in fp16 on the available GPU
you want small, swappable adapters instead of a full model copy
GPU memory allows loading the base model without quantization
avoid_when: the base model does not fit in GPU memory without quantization (use QLoRA instead)
training a <1B model where full fine-tuning is preferable

steps: Load the base model with AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto") and the tokenizer; set tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token.
Build a LoraConfig (task_type=CAUSAL_LM, r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules on attention projections, bias="none") and wrap the model with get_peft_model.
Call model.print_trainable_parameters() and confirm only <1% of params are trainable (e.g. ~13.6M / 8B ~= 0.17%).
Tokenize the dataset (truncation, max_length, padding) and remove original columns.

Configure TrainingArguments (num_train_epochs, per_device_train_batch_size, gradient_accumulation_steps, learning_rate=2e-4, fp16=True, save_strategy="epoch") and build a Trainer whose collator sets labels = input_ids.
Run trainer.train(), then model.save_pretrained(adapter_dir) to persist the adapter only.

validation: print_trainable_parameters() reports >0 trainable params (~0.17% for an 8B model)
Training loss decreases over logging steps
The saved adapter directory contains adapter_config.json and adapter_model.safetensors
recovery: CUDA OOM -> enable gradient_checkpointing, reduce per_device_train_batch_size to 1 and raise gradient_accumulation_steps, lower LoRA rank, target fewer modules, or switch to QLoRA
Loss flat / not decreasing -> lower learning_rate to 1e-4, verify the adapter is active, and check tokenized data formatting
NaN loss -> use bf16=True instead of fp16, or lower learning_rate to 5e-5
trainable params: 0 -> confirm target_modules match the architecture and call model.train()

capabilities.title: Fine-tune a large LLM with QLoRA (4-bit)
capabilities.summary: Load a 4-bit quantized base model and train a LoRA adapter so large models fit on limited GPU memory.

when: fine-tuning a large model (e.g. 70B) on a single 24GB GPU
GPU memory is the primary constraint
a ~5% quality trade-off vs full fine-tuning is acceptable
avoid_when: memory is not the constraint and full-precision LoRA already fits (avoid the QLoRA quality and speed cost)

steps: Build a BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4", bnb_4bit_compute_dtype="bfloat16", bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True).
Load the base model with AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., quantization_config=bnb_config, device_map="auto").
Call prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model) to enable gradient checkpointing and cast layers for stable k-bit training.
Build a LoraConfig with a higher rank for large models (r=64, lora_alpha=128, lora_dropout=0.1, target attention + MLP modules, bias="none", task_type="CAUSAL_LM") and wrap with get_peft_model.
Train with the same Trainer/TrainingArguments flow as standard LoRA; the 4-bit base plus LoRA adapter now fits on a single 24GB GPU.

validation: The quantized model loads in 4-bit without CUDA OOM
print_trainable_parameters() shows the expected small trainable percentage
Training loss decreases over logging steps
recovery: OOM even at 4-bit -> prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model, use_gradient_checkpointing=True), reduce batch size and raise gradient accumulation, or lower LoRA rank
NaN loss -> switch to bf16 and lower the learning rate
bitsandbytes 'CUDA Setup failed' -> reinstall bitsandbytes matching the installed CUDA version (or compile from source for that CUDA)
expected_outcomes: A 70B model fits on a single 24GB GPU (Llama 3.1 8B QLoRA r=16 uses ~6 GB)
~5% quality trade-off and ~0.84x training speed vs full fine-tuning

capabilities.title: Load, merge, and serve LoRA adapters
capabilities.summary: Load a trained adapter onto its base, merge it for deployment, or hot-swap multiple adapters at runtime.

when: deploying a trained LoRA adapter for inference
you want to remove adapter overhead by merging into the base model
serving multiple task-specific adapters from one base model
avoid_when: you still need to switch adapters at runtime — do NOT merge, since merge_and_unload bakes a single adapter into the base

steps: Load the adapter with AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(adapter_dir, device_map="auto") (recommended), or PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, adapter_dir).
For single-adapter deployment, call merged_model = model.merge_and_unload(), then merged_model.save_pretrained(dir) and tokenizer.save_pretrained(dir); optionally push_to_hub.

For multi-adapter serving, load each with model.load_adapter(path, adapter_name=...), switch with model.set_adapter(name) before generate, and use `with model.disable_adapter():` to fall back to the base model.
For faster inference, merge the adapter, or serve the merged model via vLLM / enable flash_attention_2.

validation: model.active_adapters shows the expected adapter name after loading/switching
The adapter directory contains adapter_config.json and adapter_model.safetensors
The merged model generates correctly without loading the adapter separately
recovery: 'Can't find adapter weights' -> confirm adapter files exist and load the base model from PeftConfig.base_model_name_or_path first
size mismatch -> ensure the base model matches the adapter's base_model_name_or_path
Slow generation -> merge_and_unload, use vLLM, or enable attn_implementation="flash_attention_2"

capabilities.title: Diagnose an adapter that isn't training or applying
capabilities.summary: Read-only checks that confirm a LoRA adapter is attached, trainable, and active before or during a run.

when: print_trainable_parameters reports 0 or the model is not updating
training loss stays flat
verifying an adapter is active before a long training run

steps: Run model.print_trainable_parameters() and expect a non-zero trainable count (~0.17% for an 8B model).
Print model.active_adapters and confirm it lists the expected adapter name.
Iterate model.named_parameters() and print entries with requires_grad=True to confirm LoRA params are trainable.
Iterate model.named_modules() and print names containing 'lora' to confirm LoRA layers were injected.
Compare target_modules against TRANSFORMERS_MODELS_TO_LORA_TARGET_MODULES_MAPPING[model.config.model_type] to confirm they match the architecture.
Decode a dataset sample with tokenizer.decode(sample['input_ids']) to verify data formatting, and confirm model.train() mode.

validation: The report shows >0 trainable params and a non-empty active-adapter list
recovery: trainable params: 0 -> fix target_modules to match the architecture and call model.train()
empty active adapters -> re-apply get_peft_model / reload the adapter
loss flat despite trainable params -> lower learning rate and verify tokenization

capabilities.title: Choose an advanced LoRA variant (DoRA, AdaLoRA, LoRA+, rsLoRA, LoftQ)
capabilities.summary: When standard LoRA underperforms, select a variant for higher quality, adaptive rank, rank-stability, or quantization-aware init.

when: standard LoRA quality is insufficient
exploring higher-quality or adaptive PEFT variants
experimenting with different ranks (r>32) and needing stability
improving initial quality when doing QLoRA (quantization-aware init)
avoid_when: standard LoRA already meets quality targets — variants add memory and complexity for no benefit

steps: DoRA (LoraConfig(use_dora=True)) decomposes weights into magnitude and direction; ~10% more memory; best for instruction-following and quality-critical fine-tuning.
AdaLoRA (AdaLoraConfig with init_r, target_r, tinit/tfinal, deltaT) allocates more rank to important layers and can cut total params while maintaining quality.
LoRA+ uses a higher learning rate for the B matrix (~10x the A matrix) via grouped optimizer param groups.
rsLoRA (use_rslora=True) applies rank-stabilized scaling to keep behavior consistent across rank values; recommended for r>32.
LoftQ (init_lora_weights="loftq" + LoftQConfig(loftq_bits, loftq_iter)) initializes LoRA weights to compensate for quantization error, improving on standard QLoRA.

expected_outcomes: DoRA consistently outperforms LoRA on instruction-following tasks
LoftQ gives ~1-2% better final accuracy and faster convergence than standard QLoRA
